name: Night Exterior
northStar: Every recording is a place at an hour. Open on one of them, so loud and specific you can almost feel the rain.

engine.source: 4:12 a.m. in a wet cedar forest: a recordist's headlamp off, levels glowing amber, everything else moss-dark.
engine.evidence: Sound designers buy atmosphere; the library's edge is that every file records when and where it happened.

tone._why: Persuasion page for a creative audience: loud and airy, but crafted rather than raw.

benchmark.category: Sound-effects library for film and games
keep: Play is one click from the first screen
change: Peers show a generic cinematic montage; we show one real recording's spectrogram with its log

skeleton: Full-bleed spectrogram as the hero (top 70%). Headline set over the bottom-left like a film title card; one thumb-sized play button; a slate strip of recording metadata along the bottom edge.

color.from: Sodium-lamp amber of a recorder's level meters, against moss-black. Amber appears only where sound is (the spectrogram's peaks and the play control).

hero: A spectrogram of the featured clip, rendered in moss → bone → amber; the hottest frequencies are the only saturated color.
icons: No icon set: a drawn play triangle and arrows set in the body face.
controls: Round play control 72px; text links underlined 1px offset 4px; no boxes.

motion.feel: 'Hush' — a boom pole swinging slowly into place.
motion.entrance: (later) Spectrogram scrolls in from the right like a live capture.

breakthrough: No product UI above the fold at all: the first screen is one recording.
memorable: Pressing play scrolls the spectrogram in real time and the headline time ticks (4:12 → 4:13).
